target_vertical: Multi-channel ecommerce retailers and Amazon sellers (FBA/FBM); not a manufacturing tool
pricing_model: Free for all sellers (no per-user, per-order, or per-channel fees). Power features (advanced inventory control, mobile picking, multi-channel reporting) historically had paid tiers but as of 2024-2026 the core platform is fully free; Veeqo monetises via shipping label margins and Amazon Buy Shipping rates with up to 5% Veeqo Credits back.
free_trial_or_freemium: Fully free, unlimited orders, unlimited users, no label limits. Free for all sellers (not just Amazon sellers).
shopify_sync_direction: Bi-directional for inventory; orders pulled from Shopify into Veeqo, fulfillments/tracking pushed back to Shopify.
shopify_synced_entities: Products, variants, inventory levels, orders, customers, fulfillments/shipments and tracking numbers. Refunds and draft orders are not part of the core documented sync. [uncertain]
shopify_service_item_support: [uncertain] — Veeqo is a physical-goods shipping/inventory tool; non-physical service items are not a documented sync entity.
shopify_multi_store_support: Yes — multiple Shopify stores can be connected to a single Veeqo account (each added as a separate channel).
shopify_pos_support: [uncertain] — no prominent documentation of Shopify POS depth.
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: [uncertain] — no documented native handling of Shopify B2B company locations / price lists.
shopify_markets_support: [uncertain] — no specific documentation of Shopify Markets multi-market pricing / duties handling.
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants synced via SKU; SKU is the primary match key between Shopify variants and Veeqo products.
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Near real-time order import via Shopify webhooks; product/inventory updates polled approximately every 60 minutes for some channels, but Shopify inventory writes are pushed in near real-time as orders are processed.
shopify_known_limitations: Shopify App Store rating is low (~2.8/5) with frequent complaints about support latency, label issue resolution times, inability to add post-purchase items to existing orders, and tracking emails not always marking orders as fulfilled. Some users report shipping cost markups versus advertised low rates.
etsy_listing_creation_vs_sync_only: Sync-only — Veeqo syncs existing Etsy listings; listing creation in Etsy from Veeqo is not a documented feature.
etsy_inventory_sync: Inventory syncs across Etsy and other channels via Veeqo's Inventory Control. Product updates polled approximately every 60 minutes (requires opt-in toggle in channel advanced settings).
etsy_order_import: Historically automated/real-time. Due to Etsy API changes effective October 21, 2024, Veeqo no longer offers automated order management integration for new Etsy stores connected after that date. Existing connections continue to work.
etsy_synced_entities: Listings, variations (via SKU), inventory, orders, shipments (for legacy connections). Receipts and personalization data not documented.
etsy_known_limitations: No new Etsy order-management connections accepted for US sellers post-October 21, 2024. Polling-based product sync (60 min). Personalization fields and digital products handling not documented.
amazon_marketplaces: Global — US, UK, EU marketplaces (DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, etc.), CA, MX, AU, JP, and others. Each marketplace must be connected as a separate Veeqo store even when under one Seller Central account.
amazon_seller_types: FBA, FBM (Seller-Fulfilled), and Multi-Channel Fulfillment (MCF). Vendor Central support is not documented. [uncertain]
amazon_synced_entities: Listings (sync), inventory (including FBA inbound/in-transit), orders (FBA and FBM), shipments, returns. Settlements and customer messaging not prominent. [uncertain]
amazon_listing_creation: Primarily syncs existing Amazon listings; listing creation from Veeqo is limited and not the core workflow.
amazon_buy_shipping: Yes — deep native Amazon Buy Shipping integration with Amazon's negotiated rates for orders from all channels (not just Amazon). Earn up to 5% back in Veeqo Credits on eligible shipments. This is Veeqo's headline differentiator.
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: Veeqo surfaces FBA inbound inventory ('In Transit' column) and auto-transfers it to actual FBA inventory on receipt, controlled by a per-location toggle. Creation of FBA inbound shipments from within Veeqo is not the primary workflow. [uncertain]
amazon_sp_api_inbound_v2024_03_20: [uncertain] — no public documentation of migration status to Fulfillment Inbound v2024-03-20.
amazon_settlement_report_handling: [uncertain] — Veeqo is shipping/inventory focused; settlement report posting to accounting is not a documented native flow. Third-party connectors (e.g., A2X) typically handle this.
amazon_marketplace_facilitator_tax_handl: [uncertain] — not a documented Veeqo capability; handled in accounting layer.
amazon_multi_account_support: Yes — multiple Amazon Seller accounts and multiple marketplaces can be connected, each as a separate channel.
amazon_known_limitations: For Americas marketplaces (amazon.com.mx, amazon.ca) Veeqo can only fulfill from a US warehouse. Each international marketplace must be added as a separate channel. No native repricer. Limited listing creation. Some accounting/settlement workflows offloaded to third parties.
xero_supported: Native, but closed to new connections
xero_app_store_certified: Listed historically; Veeqo is not currently accepting new Xero connections as of 2025-2026. [uncertain] on current Xero App Store certification status.
xero_synced_entities: Sales invoices (per order), COGS (so gross profit shows in Xero). Bills, payments, credit notes are not documented as part of the sync. [uncertain]
xero_accounting_sync_mode: invoice_per_order — Veeqo pushes orders to Xero as individual sales invoices.
xero_cogs_journal_method: perpetual_per_movement — COGS imported into Xero per sold item to expose gross profit.
xero_known_limitations: Closed to new connections — existing Xero customers can keep using the integration but new Veeqo merchants cannot connect Xero. Sync depth is limited to invoice + COGS; bills/credit notes/payments not documented.
qb_online_supported: Yes (via TheGenieLab partner connector listed in Veeqo App Store / marketplace)
qb_desktop_supported: [uncertain] — no documented direct QuickBooks Desktop integration.
qb_app_certified: Third-party partner connector by TheGenieLab; not a Veeqo first-party Intuit App Store listing. [uncertain] on Intuit App Store certification.
qb_synced_entities: Customers, products, orders, and other records from Veeqo to QuickBooks Online via the GenieLab connector. Bills, payments, COGS journals and credit memos not explicitly documented. [uncertain]
qb_known_limitations: QBO integration is provided through a third-party partner (TheGenieLab) rather than a first-party native sync, which adds dependency on the partner for support, mapping depth, and uptime.
other_ecom_channels: Shopify, Shopify Plus, Amazon (all major marketplaces), eBay, Etsy (legacy only for new US), Walmart, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, TikTok Shop (via partner/Patchworks), Wish, Mirakl, plus various regional storefronts. 20+ direct ecommerce/marketplace integrations.
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Yes — bundles/kits decrement component stock when sold (and bundle availability is recalculated from components). Maximum 25 components per bundle; bundles cannot be nested (no bundle-within-bundle). Converting a product to a bundle is irreversible.
other_accounting_integrations: Limited — primary partners are Xero (closed to new) and QBO (via TheGenieLab). No documented native Sage Intacct, Zoho Books, MYOB, FreshBooks, NetSuite, or Wave integrations; usually handled via Zapier/Make or partner connectors.
bom_support: No — Veeqo does not offer BOMs. Bundles/kits exist for assemble-on-sale composition but are not a true manufacturing BOM.
multi_level_bom: No — bundles cannot be nested inside other bundles (no multi-level BOM).
production_orders: No — Veeqo does not have work orders, manufacture orders, routings, or operations. It is an inventory + shipping platform, not an MRP.
batch_lot_tracking: No — Veeqo does not track batch / lot numbers or expiry dates natively. Third-party add-ons like TraceLot fill this gap.
serial_tracking: Yes — serial or batch numbers can be recorded at the point of packing an order and are searchable / exportable, but not linked to lot-level inventory.
bin_location_support: Yes — bin/sublocation tracking is supported and used to optimise picking routes and stock take order.
multi_warehouse: Yes — multiple physical warehouses are supported, with inter-warehouse transfers, nearest-location fulfillment routing, and multi-warehouse reporting.
barcoding: Yes — barcode generation and label printing, plus Veeqo Scanner (PM85) and any USB/Bluetooth barcode scanner for pick, pack, stock-take, and receiving workflows.
purchase_orders: Yes — full PO lifecycle: create PO, send to supplier, receive (full or partial), book stock in. Supplier price lists and supplier-SKU mapping supported.
supplier_management: Yes — supplier records, supplier SKU mapping, supplier price lists. Lead times and MOQs are partially supported. [uncertain] on MOQ depth.
landed_cost_support: [uncertain] — Veeqo's WMS marketing mentions landed cost management as an oversight area, but a documented native landed-cost allocation (freight/duty/insurance to inventory cost) is not prominent.
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: [uncertain] — Veeqo supports multi-currency channels and orders, but per-currency inventory valuation versus single base currency is not clearly documented.
ai_demand_forecasting: Veeqo offers Reports & Forecasting that organises sales data for purchasing decisions. Whether this is true ML-based forecasting or rule/statistical forecasting is not documented as 'AI'. [uncertain]
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: PO suggestions exist via the forecasting/reports module (replenishment recommendations based on velocity), but not marketed as AI. [uncertain]
ai_natural_language_query: [uncertain] — no documented chat-style 'ask your inventory' feature.
public_api: Yes — Veeqo has a public REST API (developers.veeqo.com) covering products, orders, purchase orders, customers, allocations, shipments, locations, suppliers and more. As of May 1, 2026 API access differs by subscription plan.
webhook_event_coverage: Yes — Veeqo supports outbound webhooks with a management API. Specific event list not exhaustively re-documented here. [uncertain] on full event coverage.
integration_architecture: Native for the main marketplaces (Shopify, Amazon, eBay, Walmart, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, Etsy); partner-built or iPaaS-style for accounting (TheGenieLab for QBO, Patchworks for some channels). Zapier connector available.
zapier_make_support: Yes — Zapier connector available (and Zoho Flow, etc.). Make/n8n not officially documented as native but Veeqo's public API allows custom integration.
mobile_app: Yes — native iOS and Android Veeqo mobile app for pick, pack, ship, stock-take, and stock-receiving workflows.
mobile_barcode_scanning_app: Yes — mobile app supports phone camera and Bluetooth/USB scanner barcode scanning for pick confirmation and stock receipt. Dedicated Veeqo Scanner (PM85) wireless device is also available.
rate_limit_handling_documented: Yes for Veeqo's own API — Leaky Bucket algorithm, bucket size 100, leak rate 5 req/sec, per-key token; 429 response headers documented in developer forum. Upstream rate-limit handling for Shopify/Amazon/Xero/QBO is not externally documented in detail. [uncertain]
sync_frequency: Orders: near real-time via webhooks for most channels. Product/inventory updates: polled approximately every 60 minutes for channels like Etsy; inventory writes to channels are near real-time as orders allocate stock. Shopify orders are real-time webhook-driven.
shipping_carrier_integrations: Extensive — USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL Express, DPD, Royal Mail, Evri/Hermes, Parcelforce, Yodel, Australia Post, Canada Post, plus Amazon Buy Shipping and Amazon Shipping as a carrier. Both Veeqo-negotiated rates and bring-your-own-account supported.
shipping_label_buying: Yes — in-app label purchase with Amazon Buy Shipping (free) and other carrier accounts. Up to 5% back in Veeqo Credits on eligible shipments. This is the headline benchmark feature.
three_pl_integrations: FBA-as-3PL via Amazon MCF (Multi-Channel Fulfillment) is the primary 3PL integration. Other 3PLs (ShipBob, ShipHero, Extensiv, Deliverr) are not natively integrated; partner/iPaaS routes exist. [uncertain]
g2_rating: 4.5 / 5 on G2 based on ~47 reviews (May 2026); rating distribution heavily 5-star (~80%).
capterra_rating: Mixed — Capterra shows generally positive reviews praising free pricing and ease of use, with criticism around shipping rate markup and support resolution times. Exact star value [uncertain].
notable_customers: [uncertain] — Veeqo case studies cover SMB Amazon and multi-channel sellers; no flagship enterprise logos featured.
last_major_release: May 1, 2026 — API access tiering rolled out by subscription plan (announced on Veeqo Developer forum). Earlier in 2024-2025: shutdown of new Etsy automated order connections (Oct 21, 2024) and continued Amazon Buy Shipping enhancements. [uncertain] on exact most-recent feature release.
last_funding_event: Acquisition by Amazon, November 2021 (terms undisclosed). Prior backers included Octopus Ventures. No subsequent independent funding events.
public_status_page_uptime: [uncertain] — no widely advertised public status page URL surfaced in research.
